scheme_name: Mission on Integrated Development of Horticulture- NHM and HMNEH
description:
The Mission on Integrated Development of Horticulture is a significant initiative by the Government of India aimed at enhancing the horticulture sector in the country. 

This mission was launched in 2014. 

It is part of the National Horticulture Mission which was initially started in 2005. 

The primary objective of this mission is to promote holistic growth of the horticulture sector through area-based and regionally differentiated strategies. 

The mission aims to increase the production of horticultural crops. 

It also seeks to improve the income of farmers engaged in horticulture. 

The government has set a target to increase the area under horticulture from 25 million hectares to 30 million hectares by 2025. 

The mission focuses on various horticultural crops including fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, and medicinal plants. 

The expected increase in production is projected to be around 20 million tonnes by the end of 2025. 

The mission also aims to enhance the productivity of horticultural crops. 

The target is to achieve an average productivity of 20 tonnes per hectare by 2025. 

The benefits of the mission include financial assistance to farmers for various horticultural activities. 

Farmers can receive up to INR 1 lakh per hectare for the establishment of new orchards. 

There is also a provision for 50% subsidy on the cost of planting material. 

For irrigation facilities, farmers can receive financial assistance of up to INR 50,000 per hectare. 

The mission also provides support for the establishment of post-harvest management facilities. 

Farmers can avail of a subsidy of 40% on the cost of cold storage units. 

The eligibility criteria for beneficiaries under this mission include being a resident of India. 

Farmers must also be engaged in horticulture activities. 

There is no specific age limit for applicants. 

However, the income of the farmer should not exceed INR 2 lakh per annum. 

Educational qualifications are not a mandatory requirement for eligibility. 

The application process for the Mission on Integrated Development of Horticulture involves several steps. 

Farmers need to approach the nearest horticulture department office in their state. 

They must fill out an application form which can be obtained from the office. 

The required documents include proof of identity such as an Aadhar card. 

Farmers must also submit land ownership documents. 

A bank account statement is required to facilitate the disbursement of funds. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the horticulture department. 

The approval process typically takes about 30 days. 

After approval, the financial assistance is disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account. 

The mission operates on a continuous basis. 

There are no specific deadlines for application submissions. 

However, farmers are encouraged to apply during the planting season to avail of timely assistance. 

The implementing authority for this mission is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The National Horticulture Board is also involved in the implementation of this mission. 

State horticulture departments play a crucial role in executing the mission at the grassroots level. 

Farmers can contact the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare for further information. 

The official website provides additional resources and contact details. 

The mission has seen significant success since its launch. 

As of 2023, the area under horticulture has increased by approximately 15%. 

The production of horticultural crops has also seen a rise of around 10 million tonnes. 

The mission has contributed to the livelihoods of over 10 million farmers across the country. 

The government has allocated INR 2,000 crore for the mission in the financial year 2023-2024. 

This funding is aimed at expanding the reach of the mission to more farmers. 

The mission also emphasizes the importance of organic farming practices. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt organic methods to enhance the quality of produce. 

Training programs are conducted regularly to educate farmers on best practices. 

The mission also promotes the use of technology in horticulture. 

Farmers are trained in modern techniques such as drip irrigation and greenhouse farming. 

The government aims to increase the adoption of technology by 30% by 2025. 

The mission also focuses on women empowerment in the horticulture sector. 

Special provisions are made to support women farmers. 

Financial assistance is provided to women-led horticulture initiatives. 

The government aims to increase women's participation in horticulture by 25% by 2025. 

The mission is aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals. 

It aims to promote sustainable agricultural practices. 

The mission also addresses food security concerns by increasing the availability of nutritious food. 

Overall, the Mission on Integrated Development of Horticulture is a comprehensive initiative. 

It aims to transform the horticulture sector in India. 

The mission provides a framework for sustainable growth and development. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of the various benefits offered. 

The mission represents a significant step towards improving the livelihoods of millions of farmers. 

It also contributes to the overall economic development of the agricultural sector in India. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the progress of the mission. 

Regular assessments are conducted to ensure that the objectives are being met. 

The mission is expected to evolve with changing agricultural trends and needs. 

Farmers are urged to stay informed about the latest developments in the mission. 

This will enable them to make the most of the opportunities available. 

The Mission on Integrated Development of Horticulture is a vital part of India's agricultural policy framework. 

It reflects the government's commitment to enhancing the horticulture sector. 

The mission is designed to be inclusive and accessible to all farmers. 

It aims to create a sustainable and prosperous horticulture ecosystem in India.
